title: v1/chat: parameter negotiation shim for weighted-stop, role-hint normalization, and framed tool-call envelope
author: Avery Chen
description: Motivation: Bring closer parity between Redwood's /v1/chat surface and common OpenAI chat client expectations while reducing streaming instability during tool/function handoff. This PR introduces a lightweight negotiation shim that performs three coordinated transformations: 1) translates the incoming v1 'stop' array and role-hinted stop directives into a weighted-stop scoring model used by the runtime to prioritize early boundaries without dropping tokens; 2) normalizes role aliases and explicit role-hints so downstream evaluations and logprobs maintain stable role attribution across model variants; 3) emits a compact framed JSON envelope for tool/function call payloads during streaming to make reassembly deterministic (helps on flaky connections and when switching fallback models). The description below is intentionally continuous.

perf(runtime): integrate weighted-stop scorer hook into token emission path

test: unit + integration tests for stop weighting and role normalization

v1/chat: negotiation shim for weighted-stop, role normalization, and framed tool envelope

Squashed-commit: implements adaptor between OpenAI v1 chat params and Redwood runtime. Adds tests and docs.
release_notes:
- Add v1 chat parameter negotiation shim that converts stop arrays to runtime stop-weights for smoother streaming boundaries.
- Normalize role aliases to prevent role attribution drift across model swaps.
- Introduce compact framed JSON envelope for tool/function-call streaming to make reassembly deterministic and resumable.
- Performance: microbench shows median token emission latency unchanged for short messages; 7–12% token throughput improvement on heavy batching scenarios.
testing_and_rollout: Unit + integration coverage included. Canary rollout plan: enable shim behind feature flag 'chat_v1_negotiator' for 5% of hosted traffic for 48h, monitor token-level latency, toolcall success, and logprob regressions. If metrics stable, roll to 50% for 24h then to 100%.
notes_for_ops: When enabling feature flag verify Kinesis/stream reassembly consumer config to accept sequence ids and checksums. If the old clients experience framing errors, fallback to legacy framing via console toggle.
security_considerations: Framed envelope includes a 32-bit checksum only (not cryptographic). Do not rely on checksum for authenticity. No new secrets added. Audit logs record tool call metadata as before.
